commit.message: Watch every repository in the window, not just the first (0.4.2)

findings.title: Single `reviewing` flag now silently drops commits from sibling repositories
findings.description: `reviewing` is one boolean for the whole Session, but there is now one watcher per repository. A commit in the backend while the frontend's review is still running (these take tens of seconds to minutes) is dropped entirely — no queue, no retry — and the log line does not say which repository was skipped. With a single watcher this only lost a rapid second commit in the same repo; with N watchers it is a routine outcome of working across two projects.
findings.suggestion: Consider tracking in-flight state per repository (e.g. a `Set<string>` of roots being reviewed) so repositories do not block one another, or queueing the skipped sha for after the current run. At minimum, including the repo name and sha in the skip message would make the loss visible.

findings.title: Per-repository settings only vary the YAML half; VS Code settings stay unscoped
findings.description: The comment states configuration is per repository, but `readSettings` calls `vscode.workspace.getConfiguration("crTrack")` with no resource scope (config.ts:61) — only the `.cr-track.yaml` merge depends on `repoRoot`. In a multi-root window, folder-level overrides of `claudePath`, `model`, `effort`, `minSeverity`, and `enabled` therefore resolve identically for every repo. Related: the `enabled` gate and the CLI-path gate are evaluated against `primary` alone, so a folder that has disabled CR-Track is still watched and reviewed.
findings.suggestion: Consider passing a resource to `getConfiguration("crTrack", vscode.Uri.file(repoRoot))` so folder-level settings apply, and filtering `repos` by `settings(r.root).enabled` rather than gating on the first repository only.

findings.title: Active-editor repo match uses a prefix test with no path-boundary check
findings.description: `normalized.startsWith(root)` matches sibling directories that merely share a prefix: a file in `/work/app-legacy` resolves to the repository at `/work/app`. The longest-root-first sort does not help when the wrong repo has the longer root. `crTrack.reviewLastCommit` would then read HEAD from — and report a review against — a different project.
findings.suggestion: Consider requiring a separator boundary (or exact equality) when matching, and trimming any trailing slash on the root first.
